title: When MettleUp's gym server is down, a gym's web page says the gym may have taken its page down
what: If the gym server cannot be reached or answers with a fault, a visitor to a gym's web page sees 'This gym page is not here. The link may be wrong, or the gym has taken its page down.' That page is also kept for a minute.
expected: A short outage shows 'This page cannot open right now, please try again in a few minutes', not words that say the gym or its link is at fault.
who: visitors to gym web pages, and the gyms
fix_line: Show a separate 'cannot open right now' page for an outage, and do not keep it

title: The admin app's offline copy opens only when the internet is fully gone, not on a weak line or a server fault
what: The admin app waits for the network with no time limit before it falls back to the copy kept on the device. On a weak line the desk stares at a blank screen until the browser gives up. If our site answers with a fault page, that fault page is shown instead of the kept copy.
expected: After a few seconds with no answer, or on a fault page, the kept copy of the admin app opens so the desk can keep working.
how_often: on weak lines and during outages
fix_line: Fall back to the kept copy after a short wait or on a fault answer

title: If the answer to 'Join' is lost on a slow line, trying again makes the person check their number again and can then say the free trial is used
what: The join request is saved and the number check is used up, but the person sees 'Could not send'. Trying again says the number check failed and sends them back to step 1 to check on WhatsApp again. After that, a free trial join says the free trial was already used, and a plan join alerts the gym a second time.
expected: A repeat of the same join is recognised and shows the person the same 'You have joined' screen.
fix_line: Send a one-time id with each join and answer a repeat with the first join's result

title: A second question to the gym from the same number replaces the first one, and a resend alerts the staff twice
what: 'Ask the gym' adds a question to the open enquiry for that number by replacing the earlier question, so a person who asks two things leaves only the last one for the gym. Sending again after a lost answer also sends every staff member a second alert.
expected: Each question is kept, and a resend of the same question is saved and alerted once.
who: gyms and people asking on gym web pages
fix_line: Keep a list of questions on the enquiry and skip a repeat of the same one

title: The demo form, the join page and the friend page wait for ever on a stuck line
what: These three forms send with no time limit. On a line that hangs, the button stays greyed out and the person is never told to try again.
expected: After about 15 seconds the form says it could not send and lets the person try again, as the gym page forms already do.
who: gym owners asking for a demo, people joining, friends of members
fix_line: Add the same 15-second limit the gym page forms use

title: The join and friend pages say 'Check your internet and try again' and keep no note of why
what: When sending a join or a friend request fails in the browser, the page shows the try-again words and writes nothing down, not even in the browser's own log. It also blames the person's internet for any failure.
expected: Every try-again keeps a note of why it failed.
fix_line: Log the reason, as the gym page forms do

title: If the public websites, join pages or gym pages break, MettleUp hears it only from gyms
what: Failures on the public pages are written only to the visitor's own browser log and to the website's server log, which nobody watches and which raises no alert. Nothing checks every so often that the member site, the owner site, the join page and the gym pages open and accept a form.
expected: A regular check opens each public site and alerts MettleUp when one fails, and a rise in failed sends raises an alert.
fix_line: Add a scheduled site check and an alert on server errors

title: MettleUp cannot see how many people visit the websites or gym pages, or how the AI helper does
what: The two websites and gym pages count no visits and no taps on 'Get the app' or 'Send to phone'. Only demo requests are saved, with a member-referral label. The AI helper's answered, 'I will ask the gym' and limit-reached outcomes go only to the server log.
expected: A simple count of visits, app-link taps, demo requests and helper outcomes per day, without tracking people.
fix_line: Count visits and outcomes per day with no personal details

items.reason: No page in this area runs a scheduled job; the Worker crons (payment check, crash clean-up) belong to the server area.
